Priced rows for another day are not shown here and neither are parlays that would cross days — a card dated one day and half-filled with the next is two facts under one label. Minimum 5, maximum 25; a day with no games is an empty board, and that is correct.

calibration_warning: This card changed how it rates: it now reads this season first and pulls thin records toward the average; before the change, when it said 70-80%, those plays hit 33.3% (12 graded). That earlier record is kept apart and is not counted in the figures below. There are not enough graded College Football plays yet to say whether these confidence numbers hold up — 18 so far, and no band has reached 20. Treat every one as unproven.
board_rule: Sorted by confidence, highest first — the same order the MLB board uses: the props model's chance where it priced the prop, the player's own record at that exact line otherwise. Rows with neither sit below every row that has one.
college_note: College records are counted over the games a player appears in. College box scores list him only when he did something, so a game he played quietly can be missing — which nudges an over slightly high. That gap was measured against the NFL, where the true figure is known: a median of 0.2 percentage points and 3.8 at the 90th percentile. Short reception lines, where the gap is biggest, carry no record at all.
